title: Traffic Orbit Guard Composer: policy-driven gradual canaries with shadow calibration and quarantine lanes
creator: Mei-Lin Zhou
description:
Problem statement: Current rollout primitives allow stepwise traffic splits but lack a compact, testable policy language that ties traffic ramps to metric budgets (latency error SLOs), shadow calibration for A/B parity measurement, and an automated quarantine path for unstable variants. Teams manually configure step schedules and add ad-hoc monitors; this leads to inconsistent safety behavior across customers and frequent manual rollbacks.

Goals: Deliver a composable policy engine (Traffic Orbit Guard Composer) that lets platform operators and product engineers declare: (1) traffic split schedules (ramp, hold, decay), (2) metric guardrails with severity tiers (warning, throttle, immediate rollback), (3) shadow mirroring rules for canary vs baseline parity checks, and (4) quarantine lanes that automatically divert suspect traffic and trigger mitigation playbooks. The engine must integrate with existing rollout UI, tracing, and cost/latency dashboards, and expose a clear audit trail for compliance.

Scope: Build the policy DSL + evaluator, runtime hooks for request routing (gradual + probabilistic ramps), shadow mirroring pipeline with sample-rate controls, a quarantine routing mechanism (temporary bucket with configurable retention), and an auto-rollback actuator that can be gated by manual approval or automated SLO breach. Exclude long-term UX polish of the Console; ship with API + JSON schema + minimal Console controls for 1.22.

Design summary:
- Policy DSL: JSON-first schema with top-level sections: traffic_plan (steps with percent, duration, jitter_budget), guards (metric spec, threshold, window, action), shadow_rules (mirror_percent, sampling_key, downstream_mask), quarantine (percentage_threshold, retention, notify_webhook). Example: {"traffic_plan":[{"percent":5,"duration_s":3600,"jitter_pct":10},...]} — evaluator will expand steps into internal token-batched routing decisions.
- Safety lattice: Guards have severity levels (info/warn/fail). Warn triggers alerting and throttles advance rate; fail pauses ramp and optionally triggers rollback. Guards are composable: can combine error-rate over 1m and p99 latency over 95th expected percentile.
- Probabilistic orbiting: Instead of strictly linear ramps, the engine supports "orbiting" where traffic oscillates within a bounded range around a step to surface instability early without full exposure. Orbit parameters are configurable per-step.
- Shadow calibration: Mirror requests to candidate model with ratio and record parity metrics (token-level divergence, hallucination heuristics). Calibration jobs run aggregation and surface regression alerts to console and canary dashboards.
- Quarantine lanes: When a guard trips, a quarantined fraction of incoming requests are routed to an isolated pool where we capture full traces, model outputs, and ML-eval runs. This reduces blast radius while enabling fast postmortem.

Observability hooks: Emit rollout.trace, rollout.metric_summaries, shadow.parity, quarantine.events. Integrate with existing per-route dashboards and provide a lightweight sanity dashboard template.

Security & compliance: Audit logs for all policy changes, RBAC enforcement for who can modify release-level policies, and ability to pin policies at org-level to block dangerous global defaults.

Success criteria:
- All canary rollouts can be configured using the DSL with no additional code changes in 95% of cases for internal teams.
- Auto-rollback triggers correctly in simulated SLO breach scenarios in our staging environment (see tests).
- Shadow parity pipeline can compute token-divergence metrics for 1M requests per day at <5% additional cost overhead when sampling at 1%.
acceptance_criteria: Schema for policy DSL validated with JSON Schema and examples in docs
Runtime evaluator implements traffic_plan + jitter + orbiting and returns deterministic routing decisions for a given seed
Guards evaluated on streaming metrics with configurable windows and correct action enums (alert/throttle/pause/rollback)
Shadow mirroring implemented with sample-rate controls and parity aggregation job producing dashboardable metrics
Quarantine routing created with trace capture and retention configuration and a notification hook
End-to-end test harness that simulates an SLO breach and validates auto-rollback behavior in staging
Console: minimal edit/view UI for attaching a policy to a deployment and displaying active guard state
implementation_notes: Phase 1: DSL + evaluator + unit tests (2 sprints). Deliver JSON schema, parser, and deterministic planner.
Phase 2: Runtime hooks + shadow pipeline + quarantine router. Work with serving-runtime to add routing API (routeDecision = evaluator(seed, req_meta)).
Phase 3: Integrations: console wiring, alerting links, and per-route dashboard templates.
Prefer feature-flag rollout for rollout-of-rollout: default policies opt-in for a subset of customers initially.
Coordinate with SRE for escalation paths and on-call runbook updates before enabling auto-rollback in prod
tests: Unit: JSON schema validation & sample policy parsing
Integration: routing simulator that feeds synthetic traces and verifies percent-exposure over 10k simulated requests
Chaos: Inject synthetic latency/error into candidate model and assert quarantine triggers and rollback in staging
Shadow parity: End-to-end job that compares baseline vs candidate over 100k sampled requests and validates aggregation latency < 5 minutes
comments: 2025-10-22 Mei-Lin Zhou: Initial ticket created after design sync with PM and SRE. Draft DSL attached to Confluence. Blockers: need routing hook in runtime API (post-v1.20).
2025-10-28 Kunal Patel: PoC for evaluator complete. Deterministic planner prototype handles jitter + orbit simulation. Pushed PoC branch to gh:runtime/traffic-orbit-poc.
2025-10-30 Alice Brennan (SRE): Reviewed quarantine retention proposal — recommend 7d default and 90d for enterprise contracts. Also requested webhook retry semantics. Adding to schema.
2025-11-03 Product review (Ravi Menon): Asked for explicit cost-control knob on shadow sampling and noted product teams want a "dry-run" mode that logs decisions but doesn't route yet.

2025-11-06 Kunal Patel: Integrated guard evaluation with metrics pipeline (prometheus->ingest). Running staging tests; discovered a race when policies update mid-step, added optimistic version check to evaluator.
